source: Cambodian MAFF/agricultural extension PowerPoint-derived presentation titled "ដំណាំឪឡឹក" (Watermelon), 42 slides; no presenter, publisher, or date named on the slides reviewed. This presentation exists as two near-identical PDF copies in the source set (one with a green-themed slide design, one plain black-on-white reformat of the same 42 slides) - treat as one source, not two corroborating sources.
text:
Watermelon requires several environmental conditions to grow well.

Temperature and sunlight: the crop needs 10-12 hours of sunlight per day for good growth. Seeds can germinate across a temperature range of 15-35°C. Flower induction (bud formation) proceeds best around 20-22°C. During flowering, daytime temperature should be about 24-27°C and nighttime temperature about 27-30°C. Near harvest, temperature around 20-24°C is favorable, and fruit ripens best at 25-30°C.

Soil: watermelon does best on sandy-loam soil types; suitable soil types mentioned include sandy loam and reddish volcanic (basaltic) soil. Soil pH should be in the range of 5-6.8.

Wind, humidity, and water regime: the field needs good open air circulation. Seed germination rate is normally 75-85%. If seed is stored under conditions where moisture content rises to 45-55%, germination rate declines. Watering/irrigation should maintain adequate field moisture, and one irrigation system reference notes a water depth of about 120-180mm.
